test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in rural India in 2019-2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**19.28%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023 measures multidimensional poverty using three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• As per the report, **19.28%** (or 0.1928) of the rural population in India was living in multidimensional poverty during the period 2019–2021.
 
• This represents a significant reduction in rural multidimensional poverty compared to previous years, reflecting the impact of various poverty alleviation schemes.
 
• The MPI considers multiple deprivations that individuals face simultaneously, including indicators like nutrition, child mortality, schooling, and access to clean water and electricity.
 
• The data was released by NITI Aayog, which is responsible for tracking and reporting poverty statistics in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is based on the **global methodology developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• It includes indicators across three dimensions: health (nutrition, child mortality), education (years of schooling, school attendance), and standard of living (access to cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets).
 
• The index provides a more comprehensive view of poverty than income-based measures alone.
 
 
 
• **Rural vs. Urban Poverty:**
 
 
• Rural poverty in India has historically been higher than urban poverty due to limited access to education, healthcare, and infrastructure in rural areas.
 
• Government schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Saubhagya Scheme, and Jal Jeevan Mission** have significantly contributed to poverty alleviation in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Significance of MPI:**
 
 
• MPI serves as a tool to monitor progress towards achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 1: No Poverty.
 
• It helps policymakers identify and address specific areas of deprivation in populations.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India’s improvement in MPI contributes to the global reduction of multidimensional poverty, given its large population.
 
• The MPI approach has been adopted by many countries to track multidimensional poverty at national and subnational levels.
